payload.reason: The evidence indicates that grammatical roles such as subject position are associated with more frequent pronoun use compared to proper noun use.

claims.text: Referents in subject position have a higher tendency to be pronominalized in subsequent sentences.
The grammatical role of the current mention is more important than that of the antecedent in predicting the choice of referential form.
Pronouns are more frequently used for referring to animate referents compared to inanimate ones, indicating a role of animacy in pronoun use.
